messages.subject: Sampling Unit
parts:
I have a question about resampling for bootstrapped CIs.

In about a 900 sq-km area we surveyed all reclaimed surface mines (129
patches) for 3 species of sparrows using line transects. Depending on the
size of the patch, there could be 1-many transects.

Two observers conducted surveys, in which only a single observer surveyed
any one patch. We found that for 1 of 3 species the detection functions
were modeled better if different among observers.

For species where we detected no difference between observers (in the
detection fct), should we resample patches as well as transects, or is
simply resampling transects appropriate? My inclination is to resample
patches, as well as transects within a patch to incorporate variability
among patches as well variability among transects within a patch.

Thanks,

Duane

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Sampling Unit
parts:
Hi Duane, list,

Loosly speaking, bootstrapping is supposed to give you a handle on the variability
you would expect if you were able to repeat the survey many times on the same
population. So, to work out which levels to bootstrap you need to think about
what was randomly assigned in your design.

You sampled all of the mines, not a random sample. So there's no point in
resampling at that level. Within each mine, you presumably selected transect
locations with some element of randomness (e.g., systematic with random start
point). So you need to resample at this level. This isn't going to work too well
for the mines with very few transects, but that's life. I'm not sure how much of
a problem that will be overall -- perhaps others have some insight here?

I don't think the level of resampling is affected by whether you found observer
differences in the detection function or not.

I'd be interested to hear if others disagree.

Cheers,

- Len
